<p class="page-deck">A completed project that developed a place-based atlas for examining how estimated benefits and costs of climate action vary across UK communities.</p>

**Work type:** Project<br>
**Status:** Completed<br>
**Relationship to the lab:** Foundational prior work — Completed through the University of Edinburgh and collaborators before CCLL was established; it was not developed at SFU.<br>
**Primary theme:** [Consequences for People and Places](/research/consequences-for-people-and-places.html)

## How this work contributes to climate learning

**Primary theme:** [Consequences for People and Places](/research/consequences-for-people-and-places.html)

**Secondary connections:** [Geographies of Climate Learning](/research/geographies-of-climate-learning.html)

**Decision or problem:** How place-based evidence can make locally varying benefits and costs of climate action visible.

**Existing evidence:** Verified Atlas methods, public output and a connected publication from foundational prior work.

**Transfer conditions:** Estimates are specific to UK data, communities, scenarios and valuation choices.

**Consequences examined:** Eleven categories of benefits and costs across more than 46,000 UK communities.

**Evidence status:** Completed foundational project associated with a separately represented public tool that remains available.

**Claim boundaries:** Atlas estimates are not universal predictions and do not establish suitability for another place.

### Research facets

**Geographies:** united-kingdom<br>
**Climate domains:** mitigation<br>
**Sectors:** cross-sectoral<br>
**Methods:** place-based-modelling, spatial-analysis, data-visualization

## Research questions

- How do the estimated benefits and costs of climate action vary between UK communities?
- How can place-based evidence make local climate choices more transparent?
